newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Sept 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Sept 26.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Thursday:
* A potential security flaw has been found in electronic cash cards, which are widely used in Europe and are being tested in the United States.
* Empire Blue Cross and Blue Shield said it would seek New York State approval to convert itself into a for-profit company.
* Loral Space & Communications Ltd said it agreed to buy AT&T Corp's Skynet Satellite Services unit for $712.5 million in cash.
* The inflation-proof government bonds announced Wednesday by President Clinton do not banish risk so much as exchange one kind of risk for another, experts say.
* Sales of existing homes fell modestly in August for the third consecutive month.
* Japan's governing coalition announced a program for reorganizing the Finance Ministry.

* Genetics Institute Inc said it developed a library of genes and proteins for use in treatments, and said it struck deals with Genentech Inc and Chiron Corp for low-cost access to the genes in return for a share of profits from any resulting drugs.
* Service Corp International said it would continue to pursue an acquisition of Loewen Group Inc despite Loewen's rejection of the $3.1 billion buyout offer.
* The International Monetary Fund said it expects annual growth of about 2.5 percent in industrialized nations until the year 2000.
* A member of the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission said U.S. stock exchanges should convert stock prices to the decimal system within three years.
* Investors and analysts cite a number of potential acquirers for Lehman Brothers Holdings Inc. Even so, the rumours may be overdone. - Market Place
